questions.stem: A library written for Java 17 has `class Route<E> extends ArrayList<E>` with `public Route<E> reversed()`, which returns a new Route holding the stops in reverse order. The team rebuilds it with `--release 21`, and a caller holding a `List<String> stops` that is really a Route calls `stops.reversed().add("Z")`. What happens?

options.text: The build fails, since Route's reversed() declares a return type other than the List<E> that List.reversed() declares
options.says: an override may return a subtype; Route<E> is a List<E>, so the method compiles and overrides List.reversed()

options.text: The build fails, since a class cannot override a default method that an interface gained after the class was written
options.says: a class method with the same signature overrides a default, whenever the default was added

options.text: It compiles, and the caller gets Route's copy, since Route's method now overrides List.reversed(); the original Route is unchanged
options.says: a matching public method with a compatible return type compiles and silently overrides the new default, so List callers get the copy

options.text: It compiles, and the caller gets the JDK's reversed view, since a call through List runs List's default; Z lands at the front of the Route
options.says: the class's own method overrides the default, so the call through List runs Route's method, not the view

origin.section: A Class That Already Had These Names Runs on 21 but No Longer Compiles for It

questions.stem: A jar compiled for Java 17 contains `class Tags extends ArrayList<String>` with `public Optional<String> getLast()`, and code in the same jar calls `tags.getLast()`. Nobody recompiles it; the service is simply started on a Java 21 JVM. What happens when that call runs?

options.text: It returns the Optional as it did on 17, since the JVM links the call by name and descriptor and the clash is a rule only javac applies
options.says: the class file compiled for 17 runs on 21; the clash appears only when the class is recompiled for 21

options.text: It returns the last String instead, since on 21 the call resolves to List.getLast(), which now sits above Tags in the hierarchy
options.says: the call was compiled against getLast() returning Optional, a different descriptor from List.getLast(), so it still runs Tags's method

options.text: Loading Tags fails with a LinkageError, since the JVM checks the class against the new List interface before it runs
options.says: the JVM treats the two getLast() methods as different methods, so nothing fails at load time; only javac rejects the source

options.text: Loading Tags fails with an IncompatibleClassChangeError, since the JVM rejects a method that clashes with an inherited default
options.says: the JVM treats the two getLast() methods as different methods, so the 17-built class loads and runs on 21

origin.section: A Class That Already Had These Names Runs on 21 but No Longer Compiles for It

questions.stem: During the upgrade a handler's `rows.get(0)` was changed to `rows.getFirst()`, inside `try { ... } catch (IndexOutOfBoundsException e) { return DEFAULT_ROW; }`. `rows` is an empty ArrayList. What does the handler do?

options.text: It returns DEFAULT_ROW, since getFirst() on an empty list throws IndexOutOfBoundsException just as get(0) did
options.says: getFirst() throws NoSuchElementException on an empty collection, not IndexOutOfBoundsException

options.text: It returns DEFAULT_ROW, since the NoSuchElementException that getFirst() throws extends IndexOutOfBoundsException
options.says: NoSuchElementException is not an IndexOutOfBoundsException, so the catch doesn't match

options.text: It ends with a NoSuchElementException, since getFirst() throws one on an empty list and it is no IndexOutOfBoundsException
options.says: replacing get(0) with getFirst() changes the exception, so a catch for IndexOutOfBoundsException stops catching

options.text: It ends with a NullPointerException later, since getFirst() returns null on an empty list as firstEntry() does on a map
options.says: only the map methods such as firstEntry() return null when empty; getFirst() throws

origin.section: Ordered Collections Now Share getFirst, getLast and reversed(); Unordered Ones Don't Get Them

questions.stem: A small cache is a LinkedHashMap in insertion order. When it is full, it removes `pollFirstEntry()`. Keys k1, k2, k3 were inserted in that order; then k1 is refreshed with a new value, and then the cache is full and one entry must go. Which entry goes?

options.text: k2, if the refresh used put(k1, value), since put moves an existing key to the end
options.says: put keeps insertion order, so an existing key stays where it was

options.text: k1, if the refresh used put(k1, value), since put leaves an existing key where it was
options.says: put of an existing key changes the value and keeps the position; putLast would have moved it to the end

options.text: k1, if the refresh used putLast(k1, value), since putLast leaves an existing key where it was
options.says: putLast names a position, so it moves an existing key to the end

options.text: k3, if the refresh used putLast(k1, value), since putLast moves an existing key to the front
options.says: putLast moves the key to the end, after k3, so k2 becomes the first entry

origin.section: On LinkedHashSet and LinkedHashMap, addFirst and putLast Move an Existing Entry
